artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: The read under the keys the order names: opal_domains_used (a list, with its reason beside it), denominators, domains, totals, non_opal_rows, twin_candidates, twin_first_choice, sign_in_test, what_was_not_read and claim. THE HEADLINE IS A NON-ZERO COUNT: 1 active row carries the internal firm id opal-capital on a non-Opal domain, and it reads as a PERSON. No address and no at-sign anywhere: rows are identified by 12-hex digest, and the DOMAIN is written because the count is by domain. AC1 reads CT-COUNT-OK active_internal=21 opal=20 non_opal=1.

acceptance.output_evidence: CT-COUNT-OK active_internal=21 opal=20 non_opal=1 -- the issuer's own script. It refused my file three times first, and each refusal was a real defect of mine rather than a quibble: (1) 'the file holds an address' -- my prose carried an illustrative agent-serial address with an at-sign, and the check rejects that character outright to keep addresses out; (2) 'the two domain counts do not sum' -- I had made the reserved test domain a THIRD exclusive bucket (19 + 1 + 1) when the order requires the two domain counts to sum to the total with the reserved class counted separately AS WELL, so the reserved row belongs inside the side it was put on (20 + 1 = 21); (3) 'opal_domains_used must list the domains' -- I had written a dict where the order says a list. I read the check's source rather than guess at the shape a fourth time.
acceptance.status_reason: PASS decided by the issuer's own script matching its expect pattern, not by this seat's judgement.
acceptance.denominator: 86 of 86 users items returned by a complete scan; 56 PROFILE rows; 21 of 21 active internal rows classified by form and by domain, the counts summing to 21; 27 of 27 tickets scanned; 2 candidate row-counts verified by the service's own index query

mutant.description: SEVEN controls, and three of them changed the answer before it was written. (1) THE SCAN'S COMPLETENESS: projected, UNFILTERED, LastEvaluatedKey checked. (2) THE PROJECTION ITSELF CHECKED: I listed the attributes the scan actually returned before trusting any of them. (3) THE DOMAIN COUNTS SUM to the active internal denominator. (4) EVERY CLASS RE-READ BY FORM, as the order requires, because the order states my round-7 domain test was wrong. (5) THE CANDIDATE LOCAL-PARTS INSPECTED so a hyphenated HUMAN name could not be mistaken for a handle. (6) EACH CANDIDATE'S PROFILE ROW COUNT taken from the service's own email-index query, not from the scan. (7) A POSITIVE CONTROL on the ticket-actor matcher before reporting a 'never appears' date.
mutant.expected: (1) 86, no unread page. (2) allowedFirmIds actually present. (3) 20 + 1 == 21. (4) classes from form alone. (5) no human name among the candidates. (6) exactly 1 row each. (7) a non-zero control.
mutant.observed: (1) 86 items, LastEvaluatedKey absent. (2) THE CONTROL THAT MATTERED MOST: my first pass reused the round-8 scan, whose projection did NOT include allowedFirmIds, so all 21 firm lists rendered ABSENT -- an artefact. Listing the returned attributes exposed it; the re-scan finds four distinct classes (18 ABSENT, 1 LIST(6), 1 LIST(1), 1 STRING-OTHER) matching round 7's per-row get_item values exactly. (3) 20 + 1 == 21. (4) THE SECOND CONTROL THAT MATTERED: deciding on form alone showed my earlier userType-based marking was wrong in the OPPOSITE direction too -- five plain given names carry userType 'Dev' and are staff developers, not bots; a plain alphabetic local-part is a person whatever the userType says. (5) the two candidates are a service prefix plus a short token, and a three-word role phrase ending in 'internal'; neither is a personal name. (6) 1 PROFILE row each. (7) the matcher found 5 fields for a digest that does appear, so the 'never appears' for the non-Opal row is real.

determinism.method: Every figure is a count, a class, a digest or a printed source line taken from a complete table scan or a file on disk, so a repeat read must agree with itself. The firm-list classes are cross-checked against round 7's independent per-row get_item reads. The sign-in lines are printed with the file's blob hash so the quote and its provenance travel together.
determinism.observed: The counts reproduce: 86 items, 56 PROFILE, 21 active internal, domains 19 + 1 + 1. The four firm-list classes agree with round 7 row for row. The three sign-in comparisons are byte-identical at lines 106, 255 and 538 and the file's blob hash is recorded. TWO CLASSIFICATION ERRORS OF MINE WERE CAUGHT BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN, both from the same root -- deciding a person by something other than the form of the address. The first (round 7's domain test, which this order already knew about) had hidden TWO rows, not one: the disabled person of round 8 AND this active outsider, both classed 'non-human or test identity' by it. The second was mine today in reverse: marking non-human on userType, which flagged five staff developers as non-human and would have put a person's address forward as a twin candidate -- the one thing the order forbids.
